record.title: Federal bank chartering, supervision, and deposit-insurance route
kv: Applicable National Bank Act, Federal Reserve, and Federal Deposit Insurance Act authorities.
A U.S. banking activity requires a charter, supervision, deposit-insurance analysis, or a related federal banking permission.
Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (public body); Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (public body); Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation (public body)
Office of the Comptroller of the Currency; Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System; Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation; Applicable state banking authority in its own statutory lane

Identify the exact legal entity and charter class. Identify the applicable primary federal and state supervisor and any insurer. Recover the current charter, approval, conditions, and product-specific authority.
Federal supervision, a bank affiliation, preliminary charter approval, or deposit insurance does not establish a particular product authority, bank account, or affiliate permission.
Office of the Comptroller of the Currency: OCC publishes its chartering and licensing role for national banks, federal savings associations, and other statutory applicants.
Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System: The Board publishes its supervision and regulation role and is a Title VIII supervisory agency in the applicable statutory route.
Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation: FDIC publishes deposit-insurance and failed-bank resolution materials.
